reason: The paper centres on integrating DNA sequence with multimodal epigenomic signals.
Treatment effects over time are modelled from sequential patient data with LSTMs or transformers.
The method builds on the MASt3R backbone and a frozen DINOv3 encoder, both transformer models.
Experiments are on generated streams corroborating the theory; no real dataset is named.
The technical core is a routing concentration and convergence analysis, with experiments corroborating the theory.
Inverse folding takes a target 3D protein structure as input.
The framework adapts Med-VLP encoders with a gated cross-attention module, not a large pretrained LLM.
The method uses LLM-generated class descriptions to build anchors; client model families are not named and no CNN is mentioned.
CFP-Gen is a diffusion language model for protein sequences, i.e. a transformer-based diffusion model.
A neural PDE solver is trained to predict multiscale basis functions.
Conditional outcome distributions are estimated but the model family is not named.
The abstract names no transformer; the segmentation network with frequency-spatial modules is taken as convolutional, the label both coders share.
The model is trained end to end to predict trial-level choices and reaction times from stimuli and evaluated against benchmarks.
The model is a neural stochastic differential equation, the neural-ODE family.
The authors fine-tune a large vision-language model on SpineMed-450k.
The abstract describes a generative framework without naming a transformer.
The benchmark employs a fine-tuned vision-language model.
The paper is normative theory about convex optimisation problems and identifiability, with no learned model fitted.
The contribution is activation steering to suppress an identity shortcut, a robustness and interpretability intervention.
The contribution is a plug-and-play gradient optimizer, CAME-Grad.
The optimizer is backbone-agnostic and no model family is named.
The method uses prediction-powered inference to give high-probability guarantees on label distributions, a statistical inference approach.
An image tokenizer (autoencoder) is trained with a regularizer derived from state-space models.
A geometric deep learning framework is proposed without naming the network family.
The agent answers biomedical text questions using an LLM and knowledge graph triplets.
The paper analyses softmax attention predictors, an attention model.
The main contribution is a systematic evaluation study with the new VGMED dataset; VGRefine is secondary.
Personalisation is done by evolving a natural-language context without updating model parameters, i.e. prompting a language model.
The paper is an evaluation study over hundreds of deep mutational scans of when pLMs succeed.
The input data are noisy 2D cryo-EM projection images.
A hyperbolic mixture-of-curvature experts network is proposed with no named family.
The contribution is a scoring rule for likelihood-based multiple-choice LLM evaluation.
An LLM agent acts in a wireless network control environment.
The core task is counterfactual generation using a structural causal model, with conformal calibration as support.
The policy is diffusion-based and no transformer is named.
The method prompts the Segment Anything Model, a vision foundation model rather than a language or vision-language model.
CCL-Net modules are described but the network family is not named.
The method bridges transcriptomic perturbation signatures and molecules as jointly central inputs.
The framework combines pathology foundation models with language prompts for semantic relevance.
The method is flow matching; no equivariant network is named.
The contribution is a benchmark evaluating existing models, with no model built or trained.
The theory is applied to teacher-student neural network models.
Effects are demonstrated in navigation simulations in RatatouGym and Habitat Sim.
The paper proposes a system-level theory with analytical results, demonstrated with an RNN.
The model is a point-process GLM for estimating directed coupling between neural populations.
A Transformer-based VAE is combined with a nonparametric GLM coupling component.
ModalTune integrates new modalities with WSIs and text-encoded labels.
The framework uses a topology-aware graph tokenizer with foundation-model embeddings over network data.
TRACER is an aggregated metric over signals, with no model trained.
The method improves compositional zero-shot recognition accuracy on benchmarks.
